subject.title: [Bug]: additional legacy-state migration sources still block gateway startup after #102780 (Matrix, Memory Core, update-check state, Codex sidecar ownership)

question: Which convergence policy should OpenClaw apply to already-imported legacy migration residue in the Matrix, Memory Core, update-check, and Codex sidecar paths before another fix lands?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but persisted-state cleanup policy decides whether these residues should be archived/removed, downgraded to notices, or held under the broader legacy-state warning design.

options.title: Repair Convergence At Source
options.body: Archive to non-colliding names or remove only verified-authoritative residue across the named sources, while preserving warning-level blockers for real conflicts.

options.title: Gate Only True Blockers
options.body: Downgrade provably already-imported residue to notices so gateway readiness is not blocked, accepting that some legacy files may remain visible.

options.title: Fold Into Broad Policy
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader legacy-state warning policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90213 and pause new fixes until that decision is settled.

recommendation.title: Repair Convergence At Source
recommendation.body: Archive to non-colliding names or remove only verified-authoritative residue across the named sources, while preserving warning-level blockers for real conflicts.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged predecessor fix for the same startup-lockout class and is closest to the current convergence-policy follow-up.
